stem.en: Hydra is at the tissue level and a flatworm is at the organ level, yet both have one opening. What does this show?

text.en: A flatworm must have a second opening that is hard to see.

feedback.en: A flatworm has a single opening for food and waste, as Hydra does.

text.en: Level of organisation and number of openings are separate facts.

feedback.en: Right. Two animals can share one opening and still differ in how their bodies are organised.

text.en: Every animal with only one opening must stay at the tissue level of organisation.

feedback.en: A flatworm has one opening and has organs, so this rule fails.

text.en: An animal with tentacles is always at a higher level than one without.

feedback.en: Hydra has tentacles and is at the tissue level, while a flatworm has none and is at the organ level.

explanation.en: Hydra and a flatworm both use one opening for food and waste, but a flatworm's tissues form organs. So the number of openings and the level of organisation must be checked separately.

hints.en: Compare what the two animals share with what differs between them.
